title: Orthogonal Junk: Gradient-Orthogonality Data Selection for Continual Pre-Training on Low-Quality Data

contributions.purpose: Mitigate "brain rot" capability degradation when continually pre-training LLMs on low-quality social media data.
contributions.mechanism: Orthogonal Junk, a three-stage pipeline that computes anchor gradients from diverse capability benchmarks, scores candidate samples by gradient orthogonality to those anchors, and uses pool-weighted sampling to balance selection quality with diversity.
contributions.evaluation: On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct it yields mixed results: +2.89pp on RULER long-context understanding vs random selection (54.66% vs 51.77%) but -5.12pp on ARC-Challenge reasoning (23.21% vs 28.33%), and a perplexity baseline beats it on RULER (+8.05pp, 62.71%).
contributions.source_quote: (1) We propose Orthogonal Junk, a gradient-based data selection method for continual pre-training that selects samples with gradients orthogonal to capability-preserving anchors.

contributions.purpose: Characterize which model capabilities are most vulnerable to brain rot from low-quality data.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of degradation across capability benchmarks during continual pre-training.
contributions.evaluation: Shows brain-rot effects are task-dependent, with long-context understanding (RULER) more vulnerable than reasoning (ARC-Challenge).
contributions.source_quote: (2) We provide empirical evidence that brain-rot effects are task-dependent, with long-context understanding (RULER) more vulnerable than reasoning (ARC-Challenge).

contributions.purpose: Expose a hidden confound that distorts evaluation of data subset selection methods.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of data repetition rates arising when the selected pool is smaller than the token budget, correlated against downstream performance.
contributions.evaluation: Reducing repetition from 9.57x to 2.31x improves ARC-Challenge from 15.36% to 23.21% while RULER remains flat, showing repetition rate dominates selection quality for reasoning.
contributions.source_quote: (3) We identify data repetition as a critical confound in subset selection methods, showing that repetition rate dominates selection quality for reasoning performance.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Drawing on insights from continual learning methods such as Gradient Episodic Memory (Lopez-Paz & Ranzato, 2017) and PCGrad (Yu et al., 2020), we hypothesize that training samples whose gradients are orthogonal to an anchor gradient computed from capability-preserving examples should cause minimal interference with existing model knowledge.

notes: Mixed/negative result paper: the proposed method is outperformed by a simple perplexity baseline on RULER and degrades reasoning; abstract concludes gradient orthogonality at the LM head may not capture capability preservation. Related Work section is not on pages 1-2 (Method is Section 2); Section 2.2 also states the method filters data 'Rather than modifying gradients during training as in GEM or PCGrad ... following the data-centric approach of recent work on gradient-based selection (Zhang et al., 2026)'.
